original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Determination of the thermodynamic parameters for Hsp90 interaction with GDM and GDM congeners was performed by isothermal titration calorimetry using LV Affinity ITC microcalorimeter with gold cells (TA Instruments). For these experiments the heat shock protein Hsp90α protein, human recombinant was used (M = 22 600 g/mol; purity >90%, SinoBiological, Cat. 11445-HNCE). In each titration experiment, GDM or GDM derivatives and Hsp90 protein were dissolved in 10 mM phosphorus buffer solution pH 7.4 containing 1% DMSO. Hsp90 solution (182 μL; 30 μM; in cell) was titrated by adding 20 aliquots of 2.5 μL of ligand solution (200 μM GDM or GDM derivatives) from the syringe. After each injection, the change in heating power was recorded over a period of 300 s until equilibrium was reached. The measurements were performed at 25 °C with a stirring rate of 75 rpm. During the titration, the molar ratio of ligand to Hsp90 increased from 0.09/1 to 2.1/1. For each experiment the heat generated was recorded and integrated. Similar to previously published ITC results for Hsp90 titration [42] generation of some background heat was noticed for DMSO concentrations that did not completely match. This was accounted for by the subtraction of a linear drift value (blank) from the data obtained. The resulting data were plotted and fitted (NanoAnalyze Data Analysis 3.12.0 software, TA Instruments) according to a one-site independent binding model by non-linear multiparameter regression to calculate the dissociation constant Kd and thermodynamic standard functions describing the process of ligand binding with active site of Hsp90 macromolecule: enthalpy ΔH, entropy ΔS and Gibbs free energy ΔG.

ITC curves of Hsp90 binding interactions with ligands were described with the one-site independent binding model (solid lines).
